questions.question: Differentiate between mind and self in Symbolic Interactionism.
questions.solution_html:
• Mind is a process of thinking, while self is the awareness of identity.
  • 17a. Coser viewed conflict as functional for maintaining group cohesion. He argued that
  • conflict can strengthen social bonds and promote adaptation.
  • 17b. Structuralism analyses underlying patterns in language and culture. It reveals deep
  • structures that shape social practices.
  • 18a. Functionalism has its roots in classical sociology, especially Durkheim. It emphasizes
  • stability, order, and integration in society.
  • 18b. Conflict has both positive and negative consequences in society. It can promote social
  • change but may also create instability.
  • 19a. Parsons’ voluntaristic theory emphasizes action guided by norms and values. The
  • concept of the unit act explains the basic elements of social action.
  • 19b. Cooley argued that the self develops through social interaction. His “looking-glass self”
  • explains how individuals see themselves through others’ perceptions.
  • 20a. Conflict perspective explains social change through struggles between competing
  • groups. It highlights inequality and power dynamics in society.
  • 20b. Structuralism compares systems like language and kinship to identify patterns. Both are
  • seen as governed by underlying structures.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: seen as governed by underlying structures.
